The *Viññāṇalakkhaṇapañha* (“The Question on the Mark of Consciousness”) is a dialogue situated in the *Milindapañha* (Mil 3.3.12) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records four translations of the text in three languages, including an English translation by John Kelly [SuttaCentral].
Automated analysis by DharmaNexus detects forty-three matching passages shared between the *Viññāṇalakkhaṇapañha* and eight other Pali works, with no significant cross-language parallels detected [DharmaNexus]. The largest reuse partner is the Abhidhamma commentary *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā*, which shares seven matches totalling 1,033 characters, most prominently between segments §2.2_0–2.8 of this text and §1169_7–1169_12 of the commentary [DharmaNexus]. Within the *Milindapañha*, the text shares formulaic structural framing and phrases with other characterization dialogues, including the *Saññālakkhaṇapañha* (Mil 3.3.10), the *Cetanālakkhaṇapañha* (Mil 3.3.11), the *Phassalakkhaṇapañha* (Mil 3.3.8), and the *Vīriyalakkhaṇapañha* (Mil 3.1.12), in addition to sharing segments with the *Viññāṇanānatthapañha* (Mil 3.7.15) [DharmaNexus]. It is also aligned by DharmaNexus with canonical sutta passages concerning consciousness and sensory experience, notably the *Pāyāsi Sutta* (DN 23) and the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35) [DharmaNexus].
